blocks.text: Mustaqil egalik olmoshlari: mine, yours, hers ...

O'zbek tilida «mening kitobim» bilan bir qatorda «bu kitob **meniki**» degan shakl ham bor: `-niki` qo'shimchasi otni takrorlamaslikka yordam beradi. Ingliz tilida ham xuddi shunday ikki xil egalik olmoshi bor. 60-darsdagi **my, your, her** ... dan keyin doim ot keladi: **my** bag. Bu darsdagi **mine, yours, hers** ... esa otsiz, mustaqil ishlatiladi: The bag is **mine**. Ya'ni **mine** = «meniki», **yours** = «seniki / sizniki», **ours** = «bizniki».

Shakllarga e'tibor bering. **mine** — oxirida `-s` yo'q («mines» emas). **yours, hers, ours, theirs** — oxirida `-s` bor, lekin **apostrof yo'q**: «your's», «her's», «our's» deb yozish xato. **his** ikkala vazifada bir xil: **his** car — the car is **his**. **its** otsiz deyarli ishlatilmaydi.

items.text: This bag is **mine**, and that one is **yours**.
The house on the corner is **ours**.

blocks.text: **mine, yours** ... gapda ot o'rnida turadi: ot avval aytilgan bo'lsa, uni qayta takrorlamaymiz. «Is this your coat? — No, my coat is black» o'rniga — No, **mine** is black. O'zbekchada ham xuddi shunday: «Yo'q, **meniki** qora». Ular ega bo'lib ham (**Mine** is black), fe'ldan keyin ham (Can I use **yours**?), predlogdan keyin ham (next to **ours**) kela oladi.

items.text: Her phone is new, but **mine** is very old.
items.translation: Uning telefoni yangi, **meniki** esa juda eski.

items.text: I forgot my pen. Can I borrow **yours**?
items.translation: Ruchkamni unutib qoldirdim. **Siznikini** olib tursam maylimi?

blocks.text: Egasini so'rash uchun **whose** ishlatiladi. U ikki xil keladi. Otsiz: **Whose is this?** — Bu **kimniki**? Ot bilan: **Whose bag is this?** — Bu **kimning** sumkasi? Ko'plikda — are: **Whose are these?** / **Whose shoes are these?** Javobda odatda **mine, yours, hers** ... yoki ism bilan egalik keladi (It's Aziz's — 64-dars). **whose** ni **who's** (= who is) bilan adashtirmang: ikkalasi bir xil eshitiladi, lekin ma'nosi boshqa: **Who's** that? — U **kim**?

items.text: **Whose** shoes are these in the hall?

blocks.text: a friend of mine — bir do'stim

Ingliz tilida artikl va egalik olmoshi birga kelmaydi: «a my friend» deyish mumkin emas. Uning o'rniga **a friend of mine** ishlatiladi — «do'stlarimdan biri», «bir do'stim». Xuddi shunday: **a friend of yours / his / hers / ours / theirs**, **a cousin of hers** (uning bir xolavachchasi), **a colleague of ours** (hamkasblarimizdan biri). Farqi: **my friend** — tinglovchi biladigan aniq do'st; **a friend of mine** — ko'p do'stlardan biri, birinchi marta tilga olinadi.

items.text: **A friend of mine** is a chef in London.

blocks.text: O'zbeklarning tipik xatolari: «This book is my.» → **This book is mine.**; «Is this yours bag?» → **Is this your bag?** (ot oldida — your); «your's», «her's», «our's» → **yours, hers, ours** (apostrofsiz); «It's mines.» → **It's mine.**; «a my friend» → **a friend of mine**; «Who's bag is this?» → **Whose bag is this?**
Eslab qolish: o'zbekcha `-niki` = inglizcha **mine / yours / hers / ours / theirs**. «Meniki» desangiz — **mine**; «mening» + ot desangiz — **my** + ot.
Bog'lanish: my / your / her — 60-dars. To'rtta shakl birga (I / me / my / mine) — 62-dars. Ism bilan egalik: Whose is this? — It's **Aziz's**. — 64-dars.

examples.title: **mine** and **yours**
examples.description: **mine** — «meniki», **yours** — «seniki / sizniki». Ular otsiz ishlatiladi va otni takrorlamaslikka yordam beradi.

sentences.text: Excuse me, I think this seat is **mine**.
Is this pen **yours**? — Yes, thanks a lot!
My phone is dead. Can I use **yours** for a minute?
sentences.translation: Telefonimning quvvati tugadi. **Siznikini** bir daqiqa ishlatsam maylimi?

sentences.text: Your bag is really heavy, but **mine** is quite light.
sentences.translation: Sumkangiz juda og'ir, **meniki** esa ancha yengil.

sentences.text: Don't drink that coffee — it's **mine**!
These aren't my keys. Are they **yours**?
It's your decision, not **mine**.
If you've lost your dictionary, you can borrow **mine**.
sentences.translation: Lug'atingizni yo'qotgan bo'lsangiz, **menikini** olib turishingiz mumkin.

sentences.text: Which glass is **yours** — the red one or the blue one?
I've finished my sandwich — can I have a bit of **yours**?
sentences.translation: Sendvichimni yeb bo'ldim — **siznikidan** ozgina olsam maylimi?

examples.title: **his** and **hers**
examples.description: Erkak haqida — **his**, ayol haqida — **hers**; o'zbekchada ikkalasi ham «uniki». **his** ot oldida ham, otsiz ham bir xil.

sentences.text: Aziz has got a red bike. The blue one isn't **his**.
sentences.translation: Azizning qizil velosipedi bor. Ko'k velosiped **uniki** emas.

sentences.text: Ask Madina about the umbrella. I think it's **hers**.
sentences.translation: Soyabon haqida Madinadan so'rang. Menimcha, u **uniki**.

sentences.text: Tom and I have the same phone, so sometimes I take **his** by mistake.
sentences.translation: Tom ikkalamizning telefonimiz bir xil, shuning uchun ba'zan adashib **unikini** olib qo'yaman.

sentences.text: Sarah can't find her keys. Are these **hers**?
Don't thank me. Thank James — the idea was **his**.
sentences.translation: Menga rahmat aytmang. Jeymsga ayting — fikr **uniki** edi.

sentences.text: Dilnoza says that the black suitcase is **hers**.
Mr Brown thinks the parking space is **his**, but it isn't.
sentences.translation: Janob Braun to'xtash joyini **uniki** deb o'ylaydi, lekin unday emas.

sentences.text: When my sister moved in with me, half of my clothes became **hers**!
sentences.translation: Opam men bilan yashay boshlagach, kiyimlarimning yarmi **uniki** bo'lib qoldi!

sentences.text: I know that handwriting — this note is **his**.
My brother and I share a room, but the desk by the window is **his**.
sentences.translation: Akam ikkalamiz bitta xonada yashaymiz, lekin deraza yonidagi stol **uniki**.

examples.title: **ours** and **theirs**
examples.description: **ours** — «bizniki», **theirs** — «ularniki». Ikkalasida ham oxirida `-s`, lekin apostrof yo'q.

sentences.text: That house with the green door is **ours**.
Our garden is small, but **theirs** is huge.
sentences.translation: Bizning bog'imiz kichik, **ularniki** esa juda katta.

sentences.text: Is that dog **theirs**? It's always in our yard!
sentences.translation: Anavi it **ularnikimi**? U doim bizning hovlimizda yuradi!

sentences.text: We've got our tickets. Have Tom and Sarah got **theirs**?
sentences.translation: Biz chiptalarimizni oldik. Tom bilan Sara **o'zlarinikini** olishdimi?

sentences.text: This isn't our car — **ours** is in the car park.
The children say that the ball is **theirs**.
Their wedding was in summer, and **ours** was in autumn.
sentences.translation: Ularning to'yi yozda bo'lgan, **bizniki** esa kuzda.

sentences.text: Don't take those chairs — they're **theirs**, not ours.
sentences.translation: U stullarni olmang — ular **ularniki**, bizniki emas.

sentences.text: Our flat has two bedrooms, and **theirs** has three.
sentences.translation: Bizning kvartiramizda ikkita yotoqxona bor, **ularnikida** esa uchta.

sentences.text: When our computer broke, the neighbours let us use **theirs**.
sentences.translation: Kompyuterimiz buzilganda, qo'shnilar **o'zlarinikini** ishlatishga ruxsat berishdi.

examples.title: **Whose** is this? — It's **mine**.
examples.description: Otsiz savol: **Whose is this?** — «Bu kimniki?», **Whose are these?** — «Bular kimniki?». Javobda — mine, yours, hers, ours ...

sentences.text: **Whose** is this? — It's **mine**. Thanks!
**Whose** are these? — They're **ours**.
There's a wallet on the floor. **Whose** is it?
I found some keys in the car. Do you know **whose** they are?
sentences.translation: Mashinadan kalit topib oldim. **Kimniki** ekanini bilasizmi?

sentences.text: These books aren't mine. — **Whose** are they, then?
Is this bag yours? — No, it isn't **mine**. Ask Madina.
sentences.translation: Bu sumka siznikimi? — Yo'q, **meniki emas**. Madinadan so'rang.

sentences.text: Are these sunglasses **yours**? — Yes, they're **mine**.
**Who's** that man, and **whose** is that big car?
sentences.translation: Anavi kishi **kim**, anavi katta mashina esa **kimniki**?

sentences.text: This coat was on the chair all night. **Whose** is it?
sentences.translation: Bu palto tun bo'yi stulda turdi. **Kimniki** ekan?

sentences.text: Is this cake **ours**? — No, it's **theirs**; ours is in the fridge.

examples.title: **Whose** + noun: Whose bag is this?
examples.description: **whose** + ot — «kimning ...?»: **Whose** bag is this? — Bu **kimning** sumkasi? Ichki savolda ham: I don't know **whose** phone this is.

sentences.text: **Whose** bag is this? — Sorry, it's **mine**.
**Whose** car is parked in front of the gate?
Dad, **whose** turn is it to wash the dishes tonight?
Do you know **whose** phone is ringing?
**Whose** idea was it to go camping in the rain?
sentences.translation: Yomg'irda chodir tikib dam olish **kimning** fikri edi?

sentences.text: Remind me, **whose** birthday is it on Saturday?
sentences.translation: Eslatib yuboring-chi, shanba kuni **kimning** tug'ilgan kuni?

sentences.text: Nobody knows **whose** dog this is.
sentences.translation: Bu it **kimniki** ekanini hech kim bilmaydi.

sentences.text: I can't remember **whose** number this is.
**Who's** coming to the party, and **whose** car are we taking?
Excuse me, **whose** coats are these on the chairs?

examples.title: **a friend of mine**, a cousin **of hers**
examples.description: «a my friend» bo'lmaydi — **a friend of mine** («bir do'stim», «do'stlarimdan biri»). Xuddi shunday: a neighbour **of his**, a colleague **of ours**.

sentences.text: **A friend of mine** works at the airport.
Dilnoza is **a colleague of ours** from the Tashkent office.
Tonight I'm meeting **some old friends of mine** from school.
sentences.translation: Bugun kechqurun maktabdagi **eski do'stlarim** bilan uchrashaman.

sentences.text: Is Tom **a friend of yours**? — Yes, we went to school together.
Sarah came to the party with **a cousin of hers** from Oxford.
sentences.translation: Sara ziyofatga Oksforddagi **bir xolavachchasi** bilan keldi.

sentences.text: Bekzod and **a neighbour of his** are building a garage.
**A student of mine** has just won a national competition.
sentences.translation: **Shogirdlarimdan biri** yaqinda respublika tanlovida g'olib bo'ldi.

sentences.text: I heard the news from **an old friend of mine** in Manchester.
sentences.translation: Bu xabarni Manchesterdagi **eski bir do'stimdan** eshitdim.

sentences.text: Those people at the next table — are they **friends of yours**?
My dad met **a friend of his** at the market, and they talked for an hour.
sentences.translation: Dadam bozorda **bir oshnasini** uchratib qoldi, ular bir soat gaplashishdi.

examples.title: **my** bag → **mine**: with and without a noun
examples.description: Bitta gapda ikkala shakl: ot oldida — **my, your, her, our**; otsiz — **mine, yours, hers, ours**. O'zbekchada ham: «mening qahvam» — «meniki».

sentences.text: This isn't **my** coffee. **Mine** is the one with milk.
**Your** room is always tidy, but **mine** is a mess.
**Her** children are at school now, and **ours** are at the nursery.
Is it **your** car or **theirs**?
**Our** team won, and **theirs** lost.
**My** parents live in Tashkent. Where do **yours** live?
Aziz forgot **his** dictionary, so Madina is sharing **hers** with him.
sentences.translation: Aziz **lug'atini** unutibdi, shuning uchun Madina **o'zinikini** u bilan birga ishlatyapti.

sentences.text: That's not **their** fault; it's **ours**.
James showed me **his** photos, and I showed him **mine**.
sentences.translation: Jeyms menga **suratlarini** ko'rsatdi, men esa unga **menikilarni** ko'rsatdim.

sentences.text: If **your** phone isn't working, you can call from **mine**.
sentences.translation: Agar **telefoningiz** ishlamayotgan bo'lsa, **menikidan** qo'ng'iroq qilishingiz mumkin.

examples.title: Dialogue: after the party
examples.description: Ziyofatdan keyin uy egasi qolib ketgan narsalarni egalariga qaytaryapti: **whose**, **mine**, **yours**, **hers**, **his**, **ours**, **theirs**.

sentences.text: — What a mess after the party! **Whose** is this scarf?
sentences.translation: — Ziyofatdan keyin rosa tartibsizlik! Bu sharf **kimniki**?

sentences.text: — That's **mine**. Thanks, I nearly left without it.
— And this umbrella? Is it **yours** too?
— No, it isn't **mine**. Ask Madina — maybe it's **hers**.
— Madina, is this blue umbrella **yours**?
— Yes, thank you! And **whose** are those black gloves?
— Bekzod was wearing gloves like that. Maybe they're **his**.
sentences.translation: — Bekzod shunday qo'lqop kiyib kelgan edi. Balki **unikidir**.

sentences.text: — I'll phone him. And these plates? They aren't **ours**.
sentences.translation: — Unga qo'ng'iroq qilaman. Bu likopchalar-chi? Ular **bizniki** emas.

sentences.text: — The neighbours lent them to us, so they're **theirs**.
sentences.translation: — Ularni qo'shnilar berib turishgan edi, demak **ularniki**.

sentences.text: — OK, let's wash them and take them back to **their** flat.
sentences.translation: — Mayli, ularni yuvib, **ularning** uyiga olib borib beraylik.
